subject.title: [Feature Request] Telegram Channel: Support Thread Binding for Subagent Sessions

question: Should Telegram expose model-visible child-topic native subagent session spawning now, and should that ship through the active per-kind capability design while keeping Telegram's default top-level placement as current?
rationale: Current main has the generic binding adapter path and Telegram current-conversation binding, but child-topic creation affects visible Telegram UX, plugin capability/API shape, and session/message routing defaults.

options.title: Review or replace the active Telegram PR
options.body: Use the open Telegram forum-topic PR as the main design input, resolve conflicts and review risks, and require live Telegram proof before merge.

options.title: Defer child-topic spawning
options.body: Keep current-conversation Telegram binding only and leave this issue open until maintainers decide the visibility and API model.

options.title: Reject child-topic spawning
options.body: Close this issue and the candidate PRs as not planned if maintainers decide internal subagent work should never create Telegram topics.

recommendation.title: Review or replace the active Telegram PR
recommendation.body: Use the open Telegram forum-topic PR as the main design input, resolve conflicts and review risks, and require live Telegram proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining decision sits on the core adapter path and tool-surface policy introduced by his recent thread-binding refactor.
